rule_name: Ands: cut filler, keep load-bearing accumulation
quote: in September, and Voss gives them three weeks of dry drill
why: filler "and" joins the term-calendar fact and the instructional structure as equal weight instead of subordinating one to the other
suggestion: Marksmanship replaces archery in September, when Voss gives them three weeks of dry drill before anything gets loaded.

rule_name: The Said-Bookism Overcorrection, Vary Attribution in Long Exchanges
quote: Six is generous. Ruth's already bored.
why: fourth turn in a three-speaker exchange with zero attribution, so the reader has to infer by elimination that it is Sam speaking again
suggestion: "Six is generous," Sam says. "Ruth's already bored."

rule_name: Ands: cut filler, keep load-bearing accumulation
quote: so the count starts to matter again, and Odile burns the inside of her hand on an ejection port that same week
why: filler "and" chains an unrelated character anecdote onto a curriculum fact as if they carried equal weight, instead of starting a new sentence
suggestion: so the count starts to matter again. That same week, Odile burns the inside of her hand on an ejection port.

quote: because the scab pulls every time she opens her fingers
why: a complete, correct sentence ("She is still holding the palm up across the breakfast table in December") gets a trailing "because" clause tacked on, the exact construction the rulebook's own table cuts ("waits in the car with the engine running / because it's a return")
suggestion: The scab pulls whenever she opens her fingers. She is still holding the palm up across the breakfast table in December.

quote: for about as long as it takes him to decide something
why: "something" stands in for a specific, nameable decision (whether Aymar is right about the thrower) instead of naming it
suggestion: for about as long as it takes him to decide whether Aymar is right

quote: Shaking his head, "Nah. It escalates every year."
why: a dangling participial fragment used as a tag, not attached to any subject or verb, exactly the banned pattern in Rule 35's first example
suggestion: Kavi shakes his head. "Nah. It escalates every year."

rule_name: Crutch Phrases That Have Stopped Meaning Anything
quote: does the whole thing again with her hands
why: "the whole thing" is named directly as a crutch phrase that has stopped carrying specific meaning
suggestion: does the fifty-second hold again with her hands

rule_name: Hedge Where the Character Could Not Know, Cut Filler Everywhere Else
quote: standing four feet away when it happened
why: an unhedged precise distance during a fast physical scuffle is a measurement nobody took — this is Rule 28's own negative example ("four feet away claims a measurement nobody took") reproduced verbatim in the chapter
suggestion: standing about four feet away when it happened

rule_name: Crutch Phrases That Have Stopped Meaning Anything
quote: for a second with her bag half off her shoulder
why: "for a second" is named directly as a universal duration marker that has become filler regardless of what kind of moment is being timed
suggestion: she stands there, bag half off her shoulder, before she goes on to Japanese

rule_name: Crutch Phrases That Have Stopped Meaning Anything
quote: looks up at him for a while
why: "for a while" is named directly as a banned universal duration marker
suggestion: tips her head back to find his face

why: "something" is a vague placeholder for the specific anecdote (Odile's scar) that the very next lines actually tell
suggestion: Chloe is halfway through the story about Odile's scar

quote: she sits there trying to work out which one she was supposed to have opened with
why: states the fact that she is thinking without rendering the thought's texture, matching Rule 26's banned "she thought about that one for a while" pattern
suggestion: Which one was she supposed to have opened with — the height, the girlfriend, the rifle?

rule_name: The Said-Bookism Overcorrection, Vary Attribution in Long Exchanges
why: part of a six-turn parental exchange where four consecutive lines (181–187) carry no dialogue tag or attribution of any kind, leaving the reader to track the two speakers purely by counting lines
suggestion: "She said something," her mother says, flat.

rule_name: Ration a Character's Verbal Tic to the Moments It Characterises
why: hyper-precise incidental quantification applied to the father's mundane gesture, with no tie to an established character trait (unlike Aymar's or Kavi's counting habits), reads as the narration defaulting to exact-number reporting regardless of whose scene it is
suggestion: Her father moves the salt, puts it back, then gets up and starts stacking plates that nobody has finished with.

rule_name: Crutch Phrases That Have Stopped Meaning Anything
quote: her mother listens to the whole thing
why: "the whole thing" is named directly as a crutch phrase standing in for the specific explanation just given rather than naming it

quote: f she'd held it an inch lower she'd have—"
why: em dash; the ban applies everywhere, dialogue included
suggestion: replace with a comma or a short hyphen
